pt.description: Ativista norte-americana dos direitos civis, Rosa Parks tinha longa atuação contra a segregação racial e seu protesto em um ônibus de Montgomery, em 1955, tornou-se um marco do boicote aos ônibus da cidade e do movimento por igualdade perante a lei.

en.description: An American civil rights activist, Rosa Parks had a long record of organizing against racial segregation, and her 1955 protest on a Montgomery bus became a landmark of the city’s bus boycott and the movement for equal treatment under law.

en.description: An American professor, writer, and activist, Angela Davis has developed academic and public work on prisons, race, gender, and class, becoming an influential voice in debates on feminism, racial justice, and prison abolition.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Líder norte-americana dos direitos civis, Dorothy Height presidiu por quatro décadas o National Council of Negro Women e articulou campanhas por igualdade racial, direitos das mulheres e participação política, além de colaborar na organização da Marcha sobre Washington de 1963.

en.description: An American civil rights leader, Dorothy Height led the National Council of Negro Women for four decades and organized for racial equality, women’s rights, and political participation, while also helping organize the 1963 March on Washington.

title.en: Open Wide the Freedom Gates: A Memoir

en.description: An American civil rights organizer, Ella Baker worked with organizations including the NAACP, SCLC, and SNCC and promoted grassroots leadership that expanded direct participation by students and local communities.

en.description: An American journalist and activist, Ida B. Wells investigated and exposed lynching, participated in civil-rights and women’s-suffrage campaigns, and used research, journalism, and political organizing against racial violence.

en.description: An American educator and politician, Shirley Chisholm was the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress and sought the Democratic presidential nomination in 1972, while maintaining a legislative focus on civil rights and social policy.

en.description: An American lawyer and politician, Barbara Jordan served in the Texas Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives, gained national prominence during the Watergate impeachment proceedings, and later taught public policy.

en.description: An American abolitionist born into slavery, Harriet Tubman escaped and repeatedly returned to the U.S. South to guide others to freedom through the Underground Railroad, later assisting the Union during the Civil War and supporting women’s suffrage.

en.description: An American abolitionist and activist born into slavery, Sojourner Truth became an itinerant preacher and public speaker who advocated the abolition of slavery, women’s rights, and legal equality in the nineteenth century.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

en.description: An American journalist, writer, and organizer, Gloria Steinem became one of the best-known figures of the U.S. feminist movement from the late 1960s onward and co-founded Ms. magazine and organizations focused on women’s rights.

pt.description: Escritora e ativista norte-americana, Betty Friedan publicou The Feminine Mystique em 1963 e participou da fundação da National Organization for Women, contribuindo para a expansão do debate público sobre igualdade, trabalho e oportunidades para mulheres.

en.description: An American writer and activist, Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique in 1963 and helped found the National Organization for Women, contributing to broader public debate on equality, employment, and opportunities for women.

pt.description: Poeta, ensaísta, bibliotecária e ativista norte-americana, Audre Lorde escreveu sobre raça, gênero, sexualidade, identidade e desigualdade, articulando literatura e crítica social a partir da experiência de mulheres negras e lésbicas.

en.description: An American poet, essayist, librarian, and activist, Audre Lorde wrote about race, gender, sexuality, identity, and inequality, combining literature and social criticism from the perspective of Black and lesbian women.

pt.description: Socióloga norte-americana, Patricia Hill Collins desenvolveu pesquisas sobre raça, gênero, classe, sexualidade e nacionalidade e consolidou parte de sua contribuição teórica em Black Feminist Thought, publicado originalmente em 1990.

en.description: An American sociologist, Patricia Hill Collins has researched race, gender, social class, sexuality, and nation and consolidated a major part of her theoretical contribution in Black Feminist Thought, first published in 1990.

en.description: An American legal scholar and professor, Kimberlé Crenshaw works on civil rights, critical race theory, and feminist legal theory and coined the concept of intersectionality to analyze overlapping forms of discrimination.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Filósofa e teórica crítica norte-americana, Nancy Fraser desenvolveu trabalhos sobre justiça, reconhecimento, redistribuição, democracia e feminismo, examinando como desigualdades econômicas e de status se relacionam nas sociedades contemporâneas.

en.description: An American philosopher and critical theorist, Nancy Fraser has written on justice, recognition, redistribution, democracy, and feminism, examining how economic and status inequalities interact in contemporary societies.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Filósofa e professora norte-americana, Martha Nussbaum trabalha com ética, filosofia política, direito, direitos humanos e filosofia antiga, relacionando essas áreas a questões de justiça, dignidade e desenvolvimento humano.

en.description: An American philosopher and professor, Martha Nussbaum works on ethics, political philosophy, law, human rights, and ancient philosophy, connecting these fields to questions of justice, dignity, and human development.

pt.description: Reformadora norte-americana, Susan B. Anthony tornou-se uma das principais organizadoras do movimento pelo sufrágio feminino, além de participar de campanhas abolicionistas e por direitos de propriedade e educação para mulheres.

en.description: An American reformer, Susan B. Anthony became one of the leading organizers of the women’s suffrage movement and also participated in antislavery campaigns and efforts for women’s property and education rights.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Reformadora e teórica norte-americana, Elizabeth Cady Stanton organizou a Convenção de Seneca Falls de 1848, coescreveu a Declaration of Sentiments e atuou por sufrágio, direitos legais das mulheres e abolição da escravidão.

en.description: An American reformer and theorist, Elizabeth Cady Stanton organized the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention, co-authored the Declaration of Sentiments, and campaigned for suffrage, women’s legal rights, and the abolition of slavery.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Abolicionista, pregadora quaker e defensora dos direitos das mulheres, Lucretia Mott participou da organização da Convenção de Seneca Falls de 1848 e dedicou décadas a campanhas contra a escravidão e pela igualdade civil.

en.description: An American abolitionist, Quaker minister, and women’s-rights advocate, Lucretia Mott helped organize the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention and spent decades campaigning against slavery and for civil equality.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

en.description: An American suffragist and political strategist, Alice Paul organized protests for the Nineteenth Amendment, founded the National Woman’s Party, and introduced the first version of the Equal Rights Amendment in 1923.

portrait.note: Local JPEG normalized proportionally from the cited reusable source; no crop applied by the staging workflow.

pt.description: Costureira e agente da independência da Nova Granada, Policarpa Salavarrieta atuou em redes de apoio aos insurgentes durante a reconquista espanhola, foi presa pelas autoridades realistas e executada em Bogotá em 1817.

en.description: A seamstress and independence activist in New Granada, Policarpa Salavarrieta worked in support networks for insurgents during the Spanish reconquest, was arrested by royalist authorities, and was executed in Bogotá in 1817.

portrait.note: Retrato histórico de 1855; obra em domínio público.

pt.role: Ativista indígena e de direitos humanos
pt.description: Ativista guatemalteca do povo maia k'iche', Rigoberta Menchú tornou-se conhecida por sua atuação em direitos indígenas, direitos das mulheres e justiça social e recebeu o Prêmio Nobel da Paz em 1992.

en.description: A Guatemalan K'iche' Maya activist, Rigoberta Menchú became known for work on Indigenous rights, women's rights, and social justice and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.

portrait.note: Retrato de 1994 dedicado ao domínio público pelo autor via CC0.

pt.role: Ativista ambiental e de direitos indígenas
pt.description: Liderança indígena lenca e ativista hondurenha, Berta Cáceres cofundou o COPINH e organizou resistência comunitária a projetos que afetavam territórios indígenas, incluindo a barragem de Agua Zarca; recebeu o Goldman Environmental Prize em 2015.

en.description: A Lenca Indigenous leader and Honduran activist, Berta Cáceres co-founded COPINH and organized community resistance to projects affecting Indigenous territories, including the Agua Zarca dam; she received the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2015.

portrait.note: Frame de homenagem produzido pela ONU Meio Ambiente, licenciado CC BY 3.0.

pt.description: Ativista boliviana ligada às comunidades mineiras, Domitila Barrios de Chungara participou do Comitê de Amas de Casa de Siglo XX, denunciou repressão política e condições de vida nas minas e tornou-se referência na organização de mulheres trabalhadoras.

en.description: A Bolivian activist rooted in mining communities, Domitila Barrios de Chungara participated in the Siglo XX Housewives' Committee, denounced political repression and living conditions in mining areas, and became a prominent organizer of working women.

portrait.note: Retrato gráfico de Domitila Barrios, licenciado CC BY-SA 4.0.

pt.description: Advogada e ex-secretária de Inclusão Social de El Salvador, Vanda Pignato esteve à frente da criação do programa Ciudad Mujer, que reuniu em centros integrados serviços de saúde, capacitação, atenção à violência e apoio econômico para mulheres.

en.description: A lawyer and former Minister of Social Inclusion of El Salvador, Vanda Pignato led the creation of Ciudad Mujer, an integrated service-center program providing health, training, violence-response, and economic-support services for women.

portrait.sourceName: Wikimedia Commons / Presidency of El Salvador
portrait.note: Foto de 2015 da Presidência de El Salvador, disponibilizada em CC0.

pt.description: Bióloga e ativista brasileira, Bertha Lutz foi uma das principais articuladoras do sufrágio feminino no país, fundou a Federação Brasileira pelo Progresso Feminino e assumiu mandato de deputada federal em 1936.

en.description: A Brazilian biologist and activist, Bertha Lutz was a leading organizer for women's suffrage in Brazil, founded the Brazilian Federation for Women's Progress, and took office as a federal deputy in 1936.

portrait.note: Retrato do acervo do Arquivo Nacional em domínio público.

pt.description: Psiquiatra brasileira, Nise da Silveira rejeitou métodos como lobotomia e eletrochoque no tratamento psiquiátrico e desenvolveu práticas de terapia ocupacional baseadas em expressão artística, contribuindo para novas abordagens em saúde mental.

en.description: A Brazilian psychiatrist, Nise da Silveira rejected treatments such as lobotomy and electroshock and developed occupational-therapy practices centered on artistic expression, contributing to alternative approaches in mental health care.

portrait.note: Fotografia histórica anterior a 1989, disponibilizada em domínio público no Commons.

pt.description: Escritora brasileira, Carolina Maria de Jesus registrou em diários o cotidiano, a pobreza e a desigualdade vividos na favela do Canindé, em São Paulo. Seu livro Quarto de Despejo, publicado em 1960, alcançou ampla repercussão.

en.description: A Brazilian writer, Carolina Maria de Jesus documented everyday life, poverty, and inequality in São Paulo's Canindé favela through her diaries. Her book Child of the Dark (Quarto de Despejo), published in 1960, gained wide recognition.

portrait.note: Retrato de 1960 do fundo Correio da Manhã, preservado pelo Arquivo Nacional e em domínio público.

pt.description: Filósofa, escritora e ativista brasileira, Sueli Carneiro é uma referência do feminismo negro no país e desenvolveu atuação pública e acadêmica sobre racismo, desigualdade de gênero, ações afirmativas e direitos da população negra.

en.description: A Brazilian philosopher, writer, and activist, Sueli Carneiro is a major figure in Black feminism in Brazil and has worked publicly and academically on racism, gender inequality, affirmative action, and the rights of Black Brazilians.

portrait.note: Foto do Festival Latinidades de 2016, licenciada CC BY 3.0 Brasil.

pt.description: Filósofa e escritora brasileira, Djamila Ribeiro é mestre em filosofia política pela Unifesp, foi secretária-adjunta de Direitos Humanos e Cidadania de São Paulo e publicou obras voltadas a feminismo negro, racismo e participação social.

en.description: A Brazilian philosopher and writer, Djamila Ribeiro holds a master's degree in political philosophy from Unifesp, served as São Paulo's deputy secretary for Human Rights and Citizenship, and has published works on Black feminism, racism, and social participation.

title.pt: O que é lugar de fala?

portrait.note: Foto de 2016 publicada pela Agência PT sob CC BY 3.0.

pt.description: Reformadora norte-americana, Frances Willard liderou a Woman’s Christian Temperance Union e defendeu sufrágio feminino, reformas trabalhistas e maior participação política das mulheres.

en.description: An American reformer, Frances Willard led the Woman’s Christian Temperance Union and advocated women’s suffrage, labor reform, and greater political participation for women.

portrait.note: Head-and-shoulders portrait published in 1906; public domain in the United States.

pt.description: Sufragista norte-americana, Carrie Chapman Catt liderou a NAWSA, participou da campanha pela 19ª Emenda e cofundou a League of Women Voters, além de atuar posteriormente em iniciativas pela paz.

en.description: An American suffragist, Carrie Chapman Catt led the NAWSA, campaigned for the Nineteenth Amendment, co-founded the League of Women Voters, and later worked in peace advocacy.

portrait.attribution: Theodore C. Marceau / National Portrait Gallery
portrait.note: 1901 portrait; public domain in the United States.

pt.description: Ativista norte-americana, Lucy Stone atuou nos movimentos abolicionista e pelos direitos das mulheres, organizou convenções nacionais e defendeu o sufrágio e a igualdade jurídica feminina.

en.description: An American activist, Lucy Stone worked in the abolitionist and women’s-rights movements, organized national conventions, and advocated women’s suffrage and legal equality.

portrait.note: Historical photographic portrait, dated between 1840 and 1860; public domain.

pt.role: Secretária do Trabalho dos Estados Unidos
pt.description: Reformadora e gestora pública norte-americana, Frances Perkins foi a primeira mulher em um gabinete presidencial dos EUA e teve papel central em políticas do New Deal, incluindo seguridade social e padrões trabalhistas.

en.description: An American reformer and public official, Frances Perkins was the first woman in a U.S. presidential cabinet and played a central role in New Deal labor and social-welfare policy.

portrait.note: 1952 portrait; original public domain and scan released under CC0.

pt.role: Diplomata e ativista de direitos humanos
pt.description: Eleanor Roosevelt atuou como primeira-dama dos Estados Unidos, defensora de direitos civis e sociais e delegada na ONU, presidindo a Comissão de Direitos Humanos durante a elaboração da Declaração Universal.

en.description: Eleanor Roosevelt served as U.S. First Lady, advocated civil and social rights, and later served at the United Nations, chairing the Human Rights Commission during the drafting of the Universal Declaration.

portrait.license: Public domain (United States; copyright not renewed)
portrait.note: 1933 portrait from the Library of Congress; public domain in the United States.

pt.role: Jurista e juíza da Suprema Corte
pt.description: Jurista norte-americana, Ruth Bader Ginsburg cofundou o Women’s Rights Project da ACLU, litigou contra discriminação sexual e integrou a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos de 1993 a 2020.

en.description: An American jurist, Ruth Bader Ginsburg co-founded the ACLU Women’s Rights Project, litigated against sex discrimination, and served on the U.S. Supreme Court from 1993 to 2020.

portrait.license: Public domain (U.S. Supreme Court official work)
portrait.attribution: Supreme Court of the United States
portrait.note: Official Supreme Court portrait, public domain as an official U.S. Supreme Court work.

pt.role: Jurista e juíza da Suprema Corte
pt.description: Jurista norte-americana, Sandra Day O’Connor serviu no Legislativo e no Judiciário do Arizona antes de se tornar, em 1981, a primeira mulher nomeada para a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos.

en.description: An American jurist, Sandra Day O’Connor served in Arizona’s legislature and judiciary before becoming, in 1981, the first woman appointed to the U.S. Supreme Court.

portrait.note: Official portrait released as a U.S. federal government work.

pt.description: Política norte-americana, Geraldine Ferraro representou Nova York na Câmara dos Representantes e, em 1984, tornou-se a primeira mulher indicada à vice-presidência por um grande partido dos Estados Unidos.

en.description: An American politician, Geraldine Ferraro represented New York in the U.S. House and in 1984 became the first woman nominated for vice president by a major U.S. political party.

portrait.sourceName: Wikimedia Commons / U.S. House of Representatives
portrait.note: 1983 congressional portrait; public domain.

pt.description: Política e ativista norte-americana, Jeannette Rankin foi a primeira mulher eleita ao Congresso dos EUA, trabalhou pelo sufrágio feminino e votou contra a entrada do país nas duas guerras mundiais.

en.description: An American politician and activist, Jeannette Rankin was the first woman elected to the U.S. Congress, campaigned for women’s suffrage, and voted against U.S. entry into both World Wars.

portrait.note: 1917 portrait; no copyright renewal and public domain.

pt.description: Enfermeira e organizadora humanitária norte-americana, Clara Barton prestou assistência durante a Guerra Civil, fundou a Cruz Vermelha Americana e apoiou causas de direitos das mulheres.

en.description: An American nurse and humanitarian organizer, Clara Barton provided aid during the Civil War, founded the American Red Cross, and supported women’s-rights causes.

portrait.note: Historical portrait published no later than 1901; public domain in the United States.

pt.description: Reformadora norte-americana, Jane Addams cofundou a Hull House, atuou por sufrágio e reformas sociais e liderou iniciativas internacionais de paz, recebendo o Nobel da Paz em 1931.

en.description: An American reformer, Jane Addams co-founded Hull House, advocated suffrage and social reform, and led international peace initiatives, receiving the Nobel Peace Prize in 1931.

portrait.note: Portrait originally published in The World's Work in 1909; public domain in the United States.

pt.description: Bióloga e escritora norte-americana, Rachel Carson trabalhou no U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service e, com Silent Spring, impulsionou o debate público sobre pesticidas, ecologia e proteção ambiental.

en.description: An American biologist and writer, Rachel Carson worked for the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and, through Silent Spring, helped drive public debate about pesticides, ecology, and environmental protection.

portrait.note: Smithsonian portrait distributed through Flickr Commons with no known copyright restrictions.

pt.description: Bióloga e ativista queniana, Wangari Maathai fundou o Green Belt Movement, articulando reflorestamento, participação comunitária, direitos das mulheres e democracia; recebeu o Nobel da Paz em 2004.

en.description: A Kenyan biologist and activist, Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement, linking reforestation, community participation, women’s rights, and democracy; she received the 2004 Nobel Peace Prize.

portrait.note: Portrait licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0.

pt.description: Ativista nigeriana, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti fundou e liderou a Abeokuta Women’s Union, mobilizando mulheres contra tributação injusta e por direitos sociais, participação política e oposição ao colonialismo.

en.description: A Nigerian activist, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti founded and led the Abeokuta Women’s Union, mobilizing women against unfair taxation and for social rights, political participation, and anti-colonial causes.

portrait.sourceName: Wikimedia Commons / National Library of Nigeria
portrait.attribution: National Library of Nigeria / unknown photographer
portrait.note: Portrait released under the CC0 1.0 public-domain dedication.

pt.description: Política malauiana, Joyce Banda foi ministra, vice-presidente e presidente do Malawi entre 2012 e 2014, além de criar organizações voltadas a empreendedorismo, desenvolvimento rural e direitos das mulheres.

en.role: Politician and former President of Malawi
en.description: A Malawian politician, Joyce Banda served as minister, vice president, and president of Malawi from 2012 to 2014 and founded organizations focused on entrepreneurship, rural development, and women’s rights.

portrait.sourceName: Wikimedia Commons / EU Election Observation Mission Malawi
portrait.license: European Commission reuse policy; attribution required
portrait.note: 2025 EU Election Observation Mission portrait; reuse permitted with European Union attribution.

pt.description: Cantora sul-africana conhecida como Mama Africa, Miriam Makeba denunciou internacionalmente o apartheid durante décadas de exílio, usando apresentações públicas e discursos na ONU em defesa de direitos civis.

en.description: A South African singer known as Mama Africa, Miriam Makeba denounced apartheid internationally during decades of exile, using performances and United Nations speeches to advocate civil rights.

portrait.note: 1991 photograph donated by the photographer and licensed CC BY-SA 3.0.

pt.description: Escritora sul-africana, Nadine Gordimer produziu romances, contos e ensaios marcados pela experiência do apartheid e participou do movimento antiapartheid; recebeu o Nobel de Literatura em 1991.

en.description: A South African writer, Nadine Gordimer produced novels, stories, and essays shaped by the experience of apartheid and participated in the anti-apartheid movement; she received the 1991 Nobel Prize in Literature.

portrait.note: Portrait licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0.

pt.role: Ativista pela paz e direitos das mulheres
pt.description: Assistente social e ativista liberiana, Leymah Gbowee liderou uma mobilização não violenta de mulheres cristãs e muçulmanas durante a guerra civil da Libéria e recebeu o Nobel da Paz em 2011.

en.description: A Liberian social worker and activist, Leymah Gbowee led a nonviolent movement of Christian and Muslim women during Liberia’s civil war and received the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize.

portrait.note: 2012 portrait licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 2.0.

pt.role: Jornalista e ativista de direitos humanos
pt.description: Jornalista iemenita e cofundadora da Women Journalists Without Chains, Tawakkol Karman organizou protestos por liberdade de expressão e democracia e recebeu o Nobel da Paz em 2011.

en.description: A Yemeni journalist and co-founder of Women Journalists Without Chains, Tawakkol Karman organized protests for freedom of expression and democracy and received the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize.

portrait.note: 2018 portrait licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0.

pt.role: Jurista e ativista de direitos humanos
pt.description: Jurista iraniana e ex-juíza, Shirin Ebadi atua em defesa de democracia, direitos humanos e direitos de mulheres e crianças; recebeu o Nobel da Paz em 2003.

en.description: An Iranian jurist and former judge, Shirin Ebadi advocates democracy, human rights, and the rights of women and children; she received the 2003 Nobel Peace Prize.

portrait.note: 2017 portrait licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0.

pt.description: Médica e escritora egípcia, Nawal El Saadawi publicou ficção e ensaios sobre direitos das mulheres, sexualidade, religião e poder e participou de campanhas públicas contra desigualdade de gênero e violência.

en.description: An Egyptian physician and writer, Nawal El Saadawi published fiction and essays on women’s rights, sexuality, religion, and power and took part in public campaigns against gender inequality and violence.

portrait.note: Photograph at the Göteborg Book Fair in 2010, licensed CC BY 3.0.

pt.description: Ativista egípcia, Huda Sha'arawi participou do movimento nacionalista de 1919, organizou mulheres em torno de direitos sociais e políticos e fundou a Egyptian Feminist Union em 1923.

en.description: An Egyptian activist, Huda Sha'arawi participated in the 1919 nationalist movement, organized women around social and political rights, and founded the Egyptian Feminist Union in 1923.

title.pt: Harem Years: The Memoirs of an Egyptian Feminist
title.en: Harem Years: The Memoirs of an Egyptian Feminist

portrait.sourceFile: Huda Sha'arawi, 1925 photo by Underwood & Underwood.jpg
portrait.note: 1925 press portrait; public domain in the United States.

pt.description: Socióloga e escritora marroquina, Fatema Mernissi pesquisou relações de gênero, sociedade civil, história islâmica e a participação das mulheres em sociedades muçulmanas, combinando trabalho acadêmico e projetos cívicos.

en.description: A Moroccan sociologist and writer, Fatema Mernissi researched gender relations, civil society, Islamic history, and women’s participation in Muslim societies, combining academic work with civic projects.

portrait.sourceFile: Fatima Mernissi 2004 Al Azm Mernissi Soroush Mernissi cropped.tiff
portrait.note: 2004 Erasmus Prize acceptance-speech portrait; VRT permission confirmed and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

pt.description: Poeta e ativista indiana, Sarojini Naidu participou do movimento pela independência, presidiu o Indian National Congress em 1925 e, após a independência, tornou-se governadora das United Provinces.

en.description: An Indian poet and activist, Sarojini Naidu participated in the independence movement, served as president of the Indian National Congress in 1925, and after independence became governor of the United Provinces.

portrait.note: 1896 portrait reproduced in The Golden Threshold; public domain.

pt.description: Diplomata e política indiana, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit participou do movimento de independência, exerceu cargos ministeriais e diplomáticos e, em 1953, tornou-se a primeira mulher eleita presidente da Assembleia Geral da ONU.

en.description: An Indian diplomat and politician, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit participated in the independence movement, held ministerial and diplomatic posts, and in 1953 became the first woman elected president of the UN General Assembly.

portrait.note: 1938 portrait by Bassano; public domain in India.

pt.description: Educadora e ativista indiana, Aruna Asaf Ali participou da Salt Satyagraha e do movimento Quit India, tornou-se símbolo da mobilização de 1942 e, após a independência, foi a primeira prefeita de Delhi.

en.description: An Indian educator and activist, Aruna Asaf Ali participated in the Salt Satyagraha and Quit India movement, became a symbol of the 1942 mobilization, and after independence served as Delhi’s first mayor.

portrait.note: Photograph from the 1940s; Commons identifies it as free of known copyright restrictions and public domain in India.

pt.role: Ativista, reformadora social e promotora cultural
pt.description: Ativista indiana, Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay participou do movimento de independência, organizou mulheres, promoveu cooperativas e teve papel importante na preservação e institucionalização do artesanato e das artes cênicas indianas.

en.role: Activist, social reformer, and cultural organizer
en.description: An Indian activist, Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay participated in the independence movement, organized women, promoted cooperatives, and played a major role in preserving and institutionalizing Indian handicrafts and performing arts.

portrait.note: Historical photograph; Commons marks it public domain in India.

pt.description: Educadora e reformadora indiana, Savitribai Phule participou da criação de escolas para meninas e grupos marginalizados, trabalhou pela educação feminina e combateu discriminações de casta e práticas sociais que limitavam mulheres.

en.description: An Indian educator and reformer, Savitribai Phule helped establish schools for girls and marginalized communities, promoted women’s education, and challenged caste discrimination and social practices restricting women.

portrait.sourceFile: First woman Teacher Savitri Bai Phule.jpg
portrait.note: Modern portrait artwork representing Savitribai Phule, released under CC0; this is not a historical photograph.

pt.description: Escritora e educadora bengali, Begum Rokeya defendeu igualdade educacional e social para mulheres, fundou uma escola para meninas muçulmanas e usou ficção e ensaios para criticar restrições impostas às mulheres.

en.description: A Bengali writer and educator, Begum Rokeya advocated educational and social equality for women, founded a school for Muslim girls, and used fiction and essays to criticize restrictions imposed on women.

portrait.license: Public domain in India and Bangladesh
portrait.note: Historical portrait made before 1932; Commons marks it public domain under Indian and Bangladeshi law.

pt.description: Ativista paquistanesa, Malala Yousafzai tornou-se uma voz internacional pelo direito de meninas e crianças à educação após enfrentar a repressão do Talibã no vale do Swat; recebeu o Nobel da Paz em 2014.

en.description: A Pakistani activist, Malala Yousafzai became an international advocate for girls’ and children’s right to education after confronting Taliban repression in the Swat Valley; she received the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize.

portrait.note: 2023 portrait at the Nelson Mandela Annual Lecture, licensed CC BY 2.0.
